title: Externally issued VC 2.0 passport credentials secured with ecdsa-rdfc-2019
description: The exchange profile for a passport credential another party issued in the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0, secured with a Data Integrity proof under the ecdsa-rdfc-2019 cryptosuite over a P-256 Multikey published in the issuer's did:web document, and committed by the exact UTF-8 bytes as issued. Verification and intake only: this repository issues nothing under it. Proof validity, issuer binding, subject binding, validity interval, status, issuer authority under a named policy and artefact availability are separate findings; an RDF proof that still holds over re-serialised bytes does not make those bytes the anchored ones.
dataModel: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model 2.0 with the owned external passport context urn:bsv:dpp:external-passport:context:1 for subject terms

artefacts.notes: Retrieved 2026-09-06 (10131 bytes); carried at packages/vsc/artifacts/w3c/credentials-v2.jsonld and served at run time from the maintained @digitalbazaar/credentials-context package, which a test holds equal to the carried bytes.
Retrieved 2026-09-06 (2609 bytes); served at run time from @digitalbazaar/data-integrity-context 2.0.1.
Retrieved 2026-09-06 (1010 bytes); served at run time from @digitalbazaar/multikey-context 2.0.1.
The data model; the pinned context above is the artefact the implementation reads.

The ecdsa-rdfc-2019 cryptosuite; implemented through the maintained @digitalbazaar/ecdsa-rdfc-2019-cryptosuite 1.3.0 and @digitalbazaar/ecdsa-multikey 1.8.0 (BSD-3-Clause) on @digitalbazaar/data-integrity 2.5.0 and jsonld-signatures 11.6.0, never a second cryptographic implementation.
The canonicalisation the suite applies, through rdf-canonize 5.0.0.
packages/vsc/artifacts/external/dpp-external-passport-1.context.jsonld: a protected context with a vocabulary base for subject terms, served from these bytes and never fetched.
packages/vsc/artifacts/external/dpp-external-passport-1.schema.json: the structural shape the profile's schema check holds a credential to.

proofSuites.keyRule: A P-256 Multikey (publicKeyMultibase prefix zDn) whose controller is the credential issuer and which the issuer's did:web document lists under assertionMethod; never the native BSV secp256k1 key, never derived by the BRC-42 rule, and never a P-384 or P-521 key, which this profile reports as unsupported rather than verified.
proofSuites.notes: Verified with the maintained suite under RDFC-1.0 canonicalisation in safe mode, so an undeclared term is a failure and a re-serialised copy still verifies.

anchoring.bytesCommitted: the exact UTF-8 bytes of the credential as issued, including its Data Integrity proof; a re-serialised copy has a different digest and is a different commitment even though its RDF proof verifies
anchoring.attestationIdRule: the credential id; a second credential under an identifier already secured is refused, never a replacement of the earlier bytes
anchoring.subjectRule: the one credentialSubject.id the credential signs; a passport identifier that differs from it is related only through an established subject-binding policy with an evidence reference
anchoring.attestationType: the credential's first type after VerifiableCredential

nativeEvidenceExtension.notes: An external credential may reference native evidence under urn:bsv:dpp:native-evidence:1; the native evidence exists first and each reference is verified independently.

mappings.externalEvent: none: an external passport credential is retained evidence about the product and drives no token operation
mappings.requires: a separately authorised native operation with its own authority and evidence

mappings.externalEvent: none: a credential from any issuer cannot move token control
mappings.requires: the current controller's authorised transfer and the recipient's acceptance

mappings.externalEvent: none: a later independent credential does not reopen a retired lineage

storage.nativeClaim: none; the credential is independent evidence
storage.originalSecured: the exact credential string as received, with mediaType, byteLength, sha256, credentialId, issuer, receivedAt, the profile identifier and the intake verification reference
storage.decoded: the strictly parsed credential, for reading and never re-serialised as the original
storage.projection: any derived document has its own identity and digest and inherits neither the original's proof nor its anchor

unsupported.reason: This repository verifies and retains external credentials; it does not issue under this profile.
The suite can verify them; this profile declares P-256 only and reports other curves as unsupported until profiled.
JCS canonicalisation is a different suite with different exact-byte properties; not selected.
Selective disclosure is selected only when a real restricted-disclosure use case names it.
One signed subject binds to one passport; a multi-subject credential is reported unsupported, never split.
The issuer is a DID string; an issuer object is unsupported rather than read for its id.
did:web with pinned documents or an explicitly bounded resolver is the initial method; others are unsupported until profiled.
No presentation protocol, challenge or holder binding is implemented.
Enveloping proofs (VC-JOSE-COSE) are a different representation; see untp-0.7.0-jose@1.
An inline context object could redefine signed terms; only the pinned context sets are accepted.
